title: Adding and subtracting fractions and mixed numbers
blurb: Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers by hand with the least common denominator, carrying and borrowing without the slips the HESI A2 sets.
question: A hospital kitchen has 5 1/4 cups of oats. The cook uses 1 3/4 cups for breakfast and 2 2/3 cups for lunch. How many cups of oats are left, and when do you need to borrow?

teach.body: Formally, fractions can be added or subtracted only when they share a common denominator: a/d + b/d = (a + b)/d. In plain English: you can only combine pieces of the same size, so first cut everything into same-size pieces (the least common denominator, LCD), then add or subtract the numerators and keep the denominator. The HESI A2 calculator has no fraction key, so this is done by hand.

teach.h: Three kinds of add and subtract
teach.caption: The denominator names the piece size; it is never added or subtracted.

head: Denominators
Multiples of the larger
LCD
teach.caption: List multiples of the larger denominator until the smaller one divides in evenly.

items: Find the least common denominator (LCD) of 3 and 4: 12.
Add the numerators, keep the denominator: 8/12 + 9/12 = 17/12.
Write as a mixed number: 17 ÷ 12 = 1 remainder 5, so 1 5/12.

teach.h: Adding mixed numbers with a carry: 3 5/6 + 1 1/4
teach.caption: An improper fraction part means you still owe a carry to the wholes.

teach.body: When the fraction you subtract is larger than the fraction you start with, borrow 1 from the whole number and write it as a full fraction with the same denominator (4/4, 12/12...). Add it to the fraction you already have. 5 1/4 = 4 + 4/4 + 1/4 = 4 5/4. Subtracting from a whole number works the same way: 6 − 2 3/8 → 5 8/8 − 2 3/8 = 3 5/8. One whole is the denominator over itself, never 10.

items: The fraction 1/4 is smaller than 3/4, so borrow 1 whole from the 5.

teach.caption: Rename to the LCD first, then decide whether to borrow. Check: 3 7/12 + 3 8/12 = 6 15/12 = 7 3/12. ✓

teach.text: Four slips the HESI A2 turns into options: adding the denominators (1/3 + 1/4 = 2/7 is wrong; it is 7/12); subtracting the smaller fraction from the larger instead of borrowing (5 1/4 − 2 3/4 → 3 1/2); borrowing 10 instead of one whole; and adding the borrowed whole to the fraction but forgetting to take 1 from the whole number.

teach.body: Priya Patel, a nursing applicant working in a hospital kitchen, starts with 5 1/4 cups of oats and uses 1 3/4 cups, then 2 2/3 cups. Used: 1 9/12 + 2 8/12 = 3 17/12 = 4 5/12 cups. Left: 5 3/12 − 4 5/12. Since 3/12 < 5/12, borrow: 4 15/12 − 4 5/12 = 10/12 = 5/6 cup. Check: 4 5/12 + 10/12 = 4 15/12 = 5 3/12 = 5 1/4. ✓

items: Add or subtract only with a common denominator; combine numerators, never denominators.
Mixed numbers: work wholes and fractions separately, then carry an improper fraction part.
Borrow 1 whole as a full fraction (4/4, 12/12...) when the fraction you subtract is bigger.
After borrowing, the whole number goes down by 1.
Simplify the answer and check it by adding back.

summary: You can now add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers by hand using the least common denominator, carrying improper fraction parts and borrowing a whole when needed. You recognize the added-denominator, no-borrow and borrow-10 slips the HESI A2 turns into wrong answers.

A.q: A nurse has 5/6 liter of solution and uses 3/8 liter. How much solution is left?

whyNot.0: 29/24 adds the fractions (20 + 9) instead of subtracting.
whyNot.1: 1/12 = 2/24 changes the denominators to 24 but leaves the numerators as 5 and 3.
whyNot.3: 11/48 uses the right numerator (11, from twenty-fourths) over the wrong denominator, 48.

whyNot.0: 7/25 adds the numerators and the denominators: (3 + 4)/(10 + 15).
whyNot.2: 7/30 changes the denominators to 30 but leaves the numerators as 3 and 4.
whyNot.3: 17/60 renames both fractions to thirtieths, then adds the denominators (30 + 30).

A.q: A 4-liter jug of distilled water is full, and 1 3/8 liters are used. How many liters are left?

whyNot.0: 3 3/8 subtracts only the whole liter and keeps the 3/8 as part of what is left.
whyNot.1: 2 3/8 subtracts the wholes correctly but copies the 3/8 instead of finding 8/8 − 3/8.
whyNot.2: 3 5/8 finds 8/8 − 3/8 = 5/8 but does not take the borrowed 1 from the 4.

B.q: A patient drank 1 2/3 cups of water at breakfast and 2 3/4 cups at lunch. How much did the patient drink in total?

whyNot.0: 3 5/7 adds the numerators and the denominators: (2 + 3)/(3 + 4).
whyNot.1: 3 1/2 multiplies the fraction parts (2/3 × 3/4 = 1/2) instead of adding them.
whyNot.3: 3 5/12 drops the whole 1 inside 17/12 instead of carrying it to the 3.

B.q: A roll had 6 1/3 yards of medical tape, and 2 5/6 yards were used. How much tape is left?

whyNot.0: 4 1/2 subtracts the smaller fraction from the larger (5/6 − 2/6) instead of borrowing.
whyNot.1: 3 1/3 borrows without first renaming 1/3 as 2/6, so it starts from 5 7/6.
whyNot.2: 9 1/6 adds the two lengths instead of subtracting.

whyNot.0: 3 7/12 subtracts the smaller fraction from the larger (9/12 − 2/12) instead of borrowing.
whyNot.2: 3 5/12 adds the borrowed 12/12 to the fraction but does not take 1 from the 5.

C.q: A patient drank 3/4 cup of milk, 1 1/3 cups of juice and 2 1/6 cups of water. What was the total intake in cups?

whyNot.1: 3 5/13 adds the numerators and the denominators of the fractions: (3 + 1 + 1)/(4 + 3 + 6).

C.q: Keisha's walking goal is 3 miles. She walked 3/4 mile in the morning and 1 5/6 miles at lunch. How much farther must she walk to reach her goal?

whyNot.1: 2 7/12 miles is the distance she has walked, one step short of the answer.
whyNot.2: 1 5/12 finds 12/12 − 7/12 = 5/12 but does not take the borrowed 1 from the 3.
whyNot.3: 1 7/12 subtracts only the whole miles (3 − 2) and keeps the 7/12 instead of taking it away.

whyNot.1: 5 − 2 1/3 = 4 3/3 − 2 1/3 = 2 2/3; 3 1/3 comes from subtracting only the whole number and keeping the 1/3.
whyNot.3: 2/3 + 1/6 = 4/6 + 1/6 = 5/6; 3/9 adds the numerators and the denominators.

reteach.title: Fractions are like coins
reteach.question: You can't add 1 quarter and 1 dime by saying "2 coins." What do you do first, and how does making change explain borrowing?

blocks.body: A quarter is 1/4 of a dollar and a dime is 1/10 of a dollar. To add them you change both to cents, a common unit: 25 + 10 = 35 cents = 35/100 = 7/20 of a dollar. That is exactly what a common denominator does. Borrowing is making change: to pay 75 cents when you hold $3 and a quarter, you break one dollar into 4 quarters. You now have $2 and 5 quarters, not $3 and 5 quarters.

items: 3 1/4 dollars − 3/4 dollar: you can't take 3 quarters from 1 quarter.
Break 1 dollar into 4 quarters: 3 1/4 becomes 2 5/4 (2 dollars and 5 quarters).

blocks.text: 1 quarter + 1 dime is not 2/14 of a dollar. Adding the denominators is like saying two coins are always worth the same.

explain.body: Find the LCD, rename each fraction, then add or subtract the numerators and keep the denominator. 3/10 + 1/4: LCD 20, so 6/20 + 5/20 = 11/20.

test.q: A patient drinks 3/10 liter of juice and then 1/4 liter of water. How much has the patient drunk in total?

whyNot.0: 4/14 adds the numerators and the denominators.
whyNot.1: 11/40 puts the twentieths numerator over 40; in fortieths the sum is 22/40.
whyNot.2: 3/40 multiplies the fractions instead of adding them.

explain.body: If the fraction you subtract is larger, borrow 1 whole from the whole number and add it as a full fraction (5/5, 6/6...) to the fraction part. 4 1/5 becomes 3 6/5.

test.q: A bag of potting soil weighed 4 1/5 pounds, and 1 3/5 pounds were used. How much is left?

whyNot.0: 3 2/5 subtracts the smaller fraction from the larger (3/5 − 1/5) instead of borrowing.
whyNot.2: 2 2/5 borrows 1 as 5/5 but forgets to add the original 1/5 (3 5/5 instead of 3 6/5).
whyNot.3: 5 4/5 adds the two amounts instead of subtracting.

explain.h: Adding mixed numbers with a carry
explain.body: Add the wholes, add the fractions with the LCD, and if the fraction sum is improper, carry its whole into the whole-number part. 2 3/4 + 1 5/8: 3 + 11/8 = 3 + 1 3/8 = 4 3/8.

whyNot.2: 3 2/3 adds the numerators and the denominators of the fractions: 8/12 = 2/3.

explain.body: A whole number has no fraction to subtract from, so borrow 1 and write it as the denominator over itself. 5 − 2 3/7: 5 = 4 7/7, then 4 7/7 − 2 3/7 = 2 4/7.

test.q: A nurse has 5 hours left in her shift and spends 2 3/7 hours on admissions. How many hours of the shift remain?

whyNot.1: 3 3/7 subtracts only the 2 whole hours and keeps the 3/7 as part of what remains.
whyNot.2: 3 4/7 finds 7/7 − 3/7 = 4/7 but does not take the borrowed 1 from the 5.
whyNot.3: 2 3/7 subtracts the wholes correctly but copies the 3/7 instead of finding 7/7 − 3/7.
